title.zh: 卷三十三 唐書9: 莊宗本紀七
title.en: Volume 33 Book of Later Tang 9: Zhuangzong Annals 7
title.raw: 卷三十三 唐書9: 莊宗本紀七 Volume 33 Book of Later Tang 9: Zhuangzong Annals 7

sentences.zh: 同光三年秋七月丁酉，以久雨，詔河南府依法祈晴。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, dingyou, Tongguang year 3: because of prolonged rain, an edict ordered Henan prefecture to pray for clear skies according to law.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou in autumn of Tongguang 3, prolonged rain led Cunxu to order Henan to pray for fair weather by statute.

sentences.zh: 滑州上言，黃河決。

translations.literal: Huazhou reported that the Yellow River had burst its banks.
translations.idiomatic: Huazhou reported a Yellow River breach.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，皇太后崩於長壽宮，帝執喪於內，出遺令以示於外。

translations.literal: On renyin the Empress Dowager died at Changshou Palace; the Emperor observed mourning within and published her testament without.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the Empress Dowager died at Changshou Palace; Cunxu mourned within and published her last testament without.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝於長壽宮成服，百官於長壽宮幕次成服後，於殿前立班奉慰。

translations.literal: On guimao the Emperor put on mourning robes at Changshou Palace; after the hundred officials had put on robes in the tent at Changshou Palace, they formed ranks before the hall to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Cunxu donned mourning at Changshou Palace; officials robed in the tent, then lined up before the hall to console him.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，宰臣上表請聽政，不允；

translations.literal: On yisi the chief ministers memorialized asking that he resume governance; it was not granted;
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the chief ministers asked Cunxu to resume court; he refused;

sentences.zh: 表再上，敕旨宜廢朝七日。

translations.literal: the memorial came again, and an edict said court should be suspended seven days.
translations.idiomatic: they petitioned again, and he ordered seven days without court.

sentences.zh: 丁未，宏文館上言：「請依《六典》，改宏文館為崇文館。

translations.literal: On dingwei the Hongwen Academy memorialized: "We ask, following the 《Six Statutes》, to change the Hongwen Academy to the Chongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the Hongwen Academy asked, per the 《Six Statutes》, to rename itself the Chongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 」 從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 時樞密使郭崇韜亡父名宏，豆盧革希崇韜指，奏而改之。

translations.literal: At the time Privy Council commissioner Guo Chongtao's deceased father's name was Hong; Dou Luge curried Chongtao's favor and memorialized to change it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao's father's taboo name was Hong; Dou Luge flattered him and had the name changed.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》載同光三年敕云：崇文館比與宏文館並置，今請改稱，頗協舊典。

translations.literal: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》 records a Tongguang 3 edict: the Chongwen and Hongwen academies had been established together; the request to rename accorded quite well with old canon.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》 cites a Tongguang 3 edict: Chongwen and Hongwen had stood side by side, and the rename fit old precedent.

sentences.zh: 蓋豆盧革曲為之說也。）〉

translations.literal: It was Dou Luge who twisted the explanation.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luge had twisted the case.)〉

sentences.zh: 洛水泛漲，壞天津橋，以舟濟渡，日有覆溺者。

translations.literal: The Luo River swelled and destroyed the Tianjin Bridge; people crossed by boat, and each day some capsized and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The Luo flooded and wrecked Tianjin Bridge; ferries ran daily and people drowned.

sentences.zh: 己酉，宰臣百官上表，請聽政；

translations.literal: On jiyou the chief ministers and hundred officials memorialized asking that he resume governance;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou ministers and officials again asked him to hold court;

sentences.zh: 又請復常膳，表凡三上。

translations.literal: they also asked that regular meals be resumed—the memorial was submitted three times.
translations.idiomatic: and three times asked him to resume regular meals.

sentences.zh: 以刑部尚書李琪充大行皇太后山陵禮儀使，河南尹張全義充山陵橋道排頓使，孔謙充監護使。

translations.literal: Minister of Punishments Li Qi was made chief commissioner for the late Empress Dowager's mountain tomb rites; Henan prefect Zhang Quanyi was made commissioner for tomb roads and supply; Kong Qian was made overseer commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi of Punishments led the dowager's tomb rites; Zhang Quanyi of Henan handled roads and supply; Kong Qian oversaw the work.

sentences.zh: 壬子，河陽、陝州上言，河溢岸。

translations.literal: On renzi Heyang and Shanzhou reported that the river had overflowed its banks.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Heyang and Shan reported river overflows.

sentences.zh: 以禮部尚書王正言為戶部尚書，以御史中丞崔協為禮部尚書，以刑部侍郎、史館修撰、判館事崔居儉為御史中丞，以尚書左丞歸靄為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Wang Zhengyan was made Minister of Revenue; censor-in-chief Cui Xie was made Minister of Rites; Punishments vice minister, History Office compiler, and acting institute director Cui Jujian was made censor-in-chief; Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Gui Ai was made Punishments vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengyan took Revenue; Cui Xie took Rites; Cui Jujian took the censorate; Gui Ai took Punishments.

sentences.zh: 陝州上言，河漲二丈二尺，壞浮橋，入城門，居人有溺死者。

translations.literal: Shanzhou reported that the river had risen two zhang two chi, destroyed the pontoon bridge, entered the city gate, and commoners had drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shan said the river rose 2.2 zhang, broke the pontoon bridge, entered the gate, and drowned townspeople.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，汴州上言，汴水泛漲，恐漂沒城池，於州城東西權開壕口，引水入古河。

translations.literal: On yimao Bianzhou reported that the Bian River had swollen and might wash away the city walls; east and west of the prefectural city they temporarily opened moat mouths to draw water into the old river.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Bian reported the Bian in flood and briefly cut moat mouths east and west of the city to send water into the old channel.

sentences.zh: 澤潞上言，自今月一日雨，至十九日未止。

translations.literal: Ze-Lu reported that from the first day of this month rain had fallen and had not stopped by the nineteenth.
translations.idiomatic: Ze-Lu said rain from the first had not ceased by the nineteenth.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以刑部尚書、判太常卿兼判吏部尚書銓事李琪為吏部尚書，依前判太常卿；

translations.literal: On wuwu Minister of Punishments and acting Director of Ceremonies with concurrent oversight of Personnel selection Li Qi was made Minister of Personnel, still acting Director of Ceremonies;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Li Qi of Punishments became Personnel minister while keeping Ceremonies;

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎、集賢殿學士、判院事盧文紀為吏部侍郎；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War, Hall of Assembled Worthies academician, and acting institute director Lu Wenji was made Personnel vice minister;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenji of War became Personnel vice minister;

sentences.zh: 以給事中李光序為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Presentation Attendant Li Guangxu was made Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangxu became Right Secretariat assistant minister.

sentences.zh: 許州、滑州奏，大水。

translations.literal: Xuzhou and Huazhou memorialized great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Hua reported major floods.

sentences.zh: 八月壬戌，詔諸司人吏，不許諸處奏薦，如有勞績，隻許本司奏聞。

translations.literal: Eighth month, renxu: an edict forbade clerks of the various offices to seek recommendation everywhere; if they had merit, only their own office might memorialize it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renxu, clerks were barred from outside recommendations; merit cases went only through their own office.

sentences.zh: 詔有司，吳越王印宜以黃金鑄成，其文曰「吳越國王之印」。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant office: the seal of the King of Wu-Yue should be cast in gold, its inscription reading "Seal of the King of Wu-Yue."
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a gold seal for the King of Wu-Yue inscribed "Seal of the King of Wu-Yue."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，帝釋服，百官奉慰於長壽宮。

translations.literal: On dingmao the Emperor ended mourning; the hundred officials offered condolences at Changshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Cunxu left mourning; officials consoled him at Changshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，客省使李嚴使蜀回。

translations.literal: On wuchen Guest Reception commissioner Li Yan returned from an embassy to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Li Yan returned from Shu.

sentences.zh: 初，帝令往市蜀中珍玩，蜀法嚴峻，不許奇貨東出，其許市者謂之「入草物」。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had ordered him to buy Shu curios; Shu law was severe and did not allow rare goods to leave eastward—what was permitted was called "entering-grass goods."
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu had sent him to buy Shu luxuries; Shu law barred rare goods from the east, allowing only what it called "entering-grass goods."

sentences.zh: 嚴不獲珍貨，歸而奏之，帝大怒曰：「物歸中夏者命之曰『入草』，王衍寧免為入草之人耶！

translations.literal: Yan obtained no curios; on returning he memorialized this, and the Emperor raged: "Goods that reach the Central Realm are called 'entering grass'—can Wang Yan escape being a man who enters the grass!
translations.idiomatic: Yan brought back no treasures and reported it; Cunxu thundered, "Goods that reach China are called 'entering grass'—is Wang Yan not a man who enters the grass!

sentences.zh: 」由是伐蜀之意銳矣。

translations.literal: " Hence his intent to attack Shu grew keen.
translations.idiomatic: " From that his will to conquer Shu sharpened.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，幸壽安山陵作所。

translations.literal: On gengchen he visited the Shou'an mountain tomb works.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he inspected the Shou'an tomb site.

sentences.zh: 鄴都大水，御河泛溢。

translations.literal: Ye capital had great floods; the Imperial Canal overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Ye flooded and the Imperial Canal burst its banks.

sentences.zh: 癸未，河南縣令羅貫長流崖州，尋委河南府決痛杖一頓，處死，坐部內橋道不修故也。

translations.literal: On guiwei Henan county magistrate Luo Guan was exiled to Yazhou; soon Henan prefecture was ordered to beat him severely once and execute him—for failing to repair bridges and roads within his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Luo Guan of Henan was sent to Yazhou, then Henan was told to flog him once and kill him for neglected bridges and roads.

sentences.zh: 及死，人皆冤之。

translations.literal: When he died everyone deemed it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the people called it unjust.

sentences.zh: 甲申，山陵禮儀使奏：「山陵封城之內，先有丘墳，合令子孫改卜。

translations.literal: On jiashen the mountain tomb rites commissioner memorialized: "Within the tomb enclosure there are old mounds; their descendants should be ordered to rebury elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the tomb commissioner reported old graves inside the enclosure and asked heirs to move them.

sentences.zh: 舊例給其所費，無子孫者官為瘞藏。

translations.literal: By old precedent they are given the expense; where there are no descendants the government buries and stores the remains.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent paid the cost; the state buried the heirless.

sentences.zh: 如是五品以上官，所司仍以禮致祭。

translations.literal: If they were officials of the fifth rank or above, the relevant office still performed rites of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-rank officials and above still received state sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔奏，大水。

translations.literal: Fengxiang reported great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang reported major floods.

sentences.zh: 己酉，中書門下上言：「據禮儀使狀，準故事，太常少卿定大行太后諡議，太常卿署定訖，告天地宗廟。

translations.literal: On jiyou the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "According to the rites commissioner's report and established precedent, the Director of Ceremonies vice director drafts the late Empress Dowager's posthumous evaluation, the Director of Ceremonies signs and fixes it, and Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples are notified.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou the Secretariat cited precedent: the Ceremonies vice director drafts the dowager's posthumous evaluation, the director signs it, then Heaven, Earth, and the temples are told.

sentences.zh: 伏準禮文：賤不得誄貴，子不得爵母，後必諡於廟者，受成於祖宗。

translations.literal: We submit that ritual texts say: the low may not eulogize the high, a son may not ennoble his mother, and posthumous titles given in the temple receive completion from the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Rites forbid the low to eulogize the high and a son to ennoble his mother; temple posthumous titles need ancestral completion.

sentences.zh: 今大行太后諡，請太常卿署定後，集百官連署諡狀訖，讀於太廟太祖皇帝室，然後差丞郎一人撰冊文，別定日，命太尉上諡冊於西宮靈座，同日差官告天地、太微宮、宗廟，如常告之儀。

translations.literal: Now for the late Empress Dowager's posthumous title, after the Director of Ceremonies signs and fixes it, let all officials jointly sign the evaluation document, then read it in the Taizu Emperor's chamber of the Imperial Temple; afterward let one aide draft the patent text, fix another day, and order the Grand Marshal to present the posthumous patent at the western palace spirit seat; the same day let officers notify Heaven, Earth, the Taiwei Palace, and the ancestral temples by the usual notification rites."
translations.idiomatic: They asked that after Ceremonies signed the dowager's title, all officials countersign, read it in Taizu's temple chamber, draft the patent, have the Grand Marshal present it at the western spirit seat, and that day notify Heaven, Earth, Taiwei, and the temples as usual."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 青州大水、蝗。

translations.literal: Qingzhou reported great floods and locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Qing reported flood and locusts.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以襄州留後李紹珙為襄州節度使，以邠州留後董璋為邠州節度使。

translations.literal: On jichou Xiangzhou acting regent Li Shaopeng was made Xiangzhou military commissioner, and Binzhou acting regent Dong Zhang was made Binzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Li Shaopeng of Xiang and Dong Zhang of Bin became their circuits' commissioners.

sentences.zh: 九月辛卯朔，河陽奏，黃河漲一丈五尺。

translations.literal: Ninth month, xinmao new moon: Heyang reported the Yellow River had risen one zhang five chi.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao new moon of the ninth month Heyang said the Yellow River was up 1.5 zhang.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，中書上言：「大行皇太后諡議合讀於太廟太祖室，其日，集兩省御史台五品巳上、尚書省四品已上、諸司三品已上官，於太廟序立。

translations.literal: On guisi the Secretariat memorialized: "The late Empress Dowager's posthumous evaluation should be read in the Imperial Temple's Taizu chamber; that day let officials of the third rank and above from the two departments, the Censorate, and the fifth rank and above from the Secretariat, and third rank and above from the various offices, line up in order at the Imperial Temple."
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the Secretariat ordered the dowager's posthumous evaluation read in Taizu's chamber with ranked officials from the two departments, Censorate, Secretariat, and ministries present.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 鎮州、衛州奏，水入城，壞廬舍。

translations.literal: Zhenzhou and Weizhou reported water entering the cities and destroying houses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Wei reported floodwater in the cities and ruined houses.

sentences.zh: 乙未，製封第三子鄴都留守、興聖宮使、檢校太尉、同平章事、判六軍諸衛事繼岌為魏王。

translations.literal: On yiwei an investiture edict enfeoffed the third son, Ye regent, Xingsheng Palace commissioner, acting Grand Marshal, co-equal chief minister, and overseer of the Six Armies and palace guards Jiji as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Jiji—third son, Ye regent, Xingsheng Palace commissioner, acting Grand Marshal, and overseer of the Six Armies—was made Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 幸壽安陵。

translations.literal: He visited Shou'an tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Shou'an tomb.

sentences.zh: 庚子，襄州奏，漢江漲溢，漂溺廬舍。

translations.literal: On gengzi Xiangzhou reported the Han River had overflowed and washed away houses.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Xiang reported the Han in flood and houses swept away.

sentences.zh: 是日，命大舉伐蜀，詔曰：

translations.literal: That day he ordered a great campaign against Shu; the edict said:
translations.idiomatic: That day he launched the Shu campaign; the edict read:

sentences.zh: 朕夙荷丕基，乍平偽室，非不欲寵綏四海，協和萬邦，庶正朔以遐同，俾人倫之有序。

translations.literal: We from of old have borne the great foundation and lately pacified the false house—not because We do not wish to cherish and soothe the four seas and harmonize the myriad states, that the orthodox calendar might reach far and human relations be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: I inherited the throne and lately crushed a rebel regime, not because I scorn peace across the realm, but to extend orthodox rule and keep human order.

sentences.zh: 其或地居陬裔，位極驕奢，殊乖事大之規，但蘊偷安之計，則必征諸典訓，振以皇威，爰興伐罪之師，冀遏亂常之黨。

translations.literal: Yet if some land lies in a remote corner and its lord stands at the height of arrogance, utterly departing from the rule of serving the great yet harboring plans of stolen ease, then We must invoke the canon and rouse imperial might, raise troops to punish crime, and hope to check parties that disturb the constant order.
translations.idiomatic: When a remote lord grows arrogant, refuses to serve the throne, and clings to stolen ease, canon and imperial might demand a punitive host to stop disorder.

sentences.zh: 蠢茲蜀主，世負唐恩，間者父總藩宣，任君統製，屬朱溫東離汴水，致昭皇西幸岐陽，不務扶持，反懷顧望，盜據劍南之土宇，全虧閫外之忳誠。

translations.literal: This Shu ruler for generations owed Tang grace; lately his father held overall frontier command and was entrusted with rule; when Zhu Wen left Bian water eastward and caused Bright Emperor to travel west to Qiyang, he did not aid support but turned to watching and waiting, seized the land and soil of Jiannan, and wholly failed the sincerity due beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler long owed Tang favor; his father once held frontier command. When Zhu Wen drove east from Bian and the Tang emperor fled west to Qiyang, they watched instead of aiding, seized Jiannan, and betrayed the frontier.

sentences.zh: 先皇帝早在並門，將興霸業，彼既會馳書幣，此亦復展謝儀。

translations.literal: The former emperor was long at Bing Gate about to raise a hegemonic enterprise; they then exchanged letters and gifts, and We too extended thanks.
translations.idiomatic: At Bing Gate the former emperor was building power; Shu sent letters and gifts, and we answered in kind.

sentences.zh: 後又特發使人，專持聘禮，彼則更不回一介之使，答咫尺之書，星歲俄移，歡盟頓阻。

translations.literal: Later they again specially sent envoys bearing betrothal gifts; they then never returned a single envoy or answered a letter within a foot—years swiftly passed and friendly alliance suddenly broke.
translations.idiomatic: Later they sent envoys with gifts, then ignored our envoys and letters until alliance rotted away.

sentences.zh: 朕頃遵遺訓，嗣統列藩，追昔日之來誠，繼先皇之舊好，累馳信幣，皆絕酬還，背惠食言，棄同即異。

translations.literal: We lately followed the testamentary charge and succeeded to rule the succession of frontier lords, pursuing past sincerity and continuing the former emperor's old friendship; again and again We sent letters and gifts, yet all replies were cut off—favor was betrayed, words eaten, shared bonds cast aside for difference.
translations.idiomatic: I followed the testament, kept old ties, and sent gift after gift, yet Shu answered none—breaking faith and casting off shared bonds.

sentences.zh: 今觀孽豎，紹據山河，委閹宦以持權，憑阻修而僭號。

translations.literal: Now this wicked stripling has succeeded to mountains and rivers, entrusts power to eunuch officials, and relies on rugged passes to usurp title.
translations.idiomatic: Now a wicked youth holds Shu, gives eunuchs power, and leans on mountains to play emperor.

sentences.zh: 早者，曾上秦王緘劄，張皇蜀地聲塵，形侮黷之言辭，謗親賢之勳德。

translations.literal: Earlier he sent a sealed letter to the Prince of Qin, inflating Shu's fame, with insulting, irreverent words slandering the merit of our kin and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote the Prince of Qin with arrogant boasts and slander of our kin and ministers.

sentences.zh: 昨朕風驅銳旅，電掃凶渠，復已墜之宗祧，纘中興之曆數。

translations.literal: When We lately drove sharp hosts like the wind and swept the wicked like lightning, We restored the fallen ancestral temple and continued the mid-restoration calendar.
translations.idiomatic: When I lately swept Liang like wind and lightning, I restored the ancestral temple and Tang's mid-restoration reign.

sentences.zh: 捷音旋報，復命仍稽，使來而尚抗書題，情動而先誇險固。

translations.literal: Victory news soon returned, yet their reply still lagged; when envoys came they still resisted in writing, and in feeling they first boasted of perilous defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Victory reports came back, yet Shu still stalled; envoys arrived defiant and boasted of their defenses.

sentences.zh: 加以宋光葆輒陳狂計，別啟奸謀，將欲北顧秦川，東窺荊渚，人而無禮，罪莫大焉。

translations.literal: Moreover Song Guangbao rashly set forth mad plans and opened separate treacherous designs, intending to look north to Qin River and east to Jing lands—among men there is no rite greater than this crime.
translations.idiomatic: Song Guangbao moreover plotted to strike Qin and spy on Jing—a crime beyond rite.

sentences.zh: 昨客省使李嚴奉使銅梁，近歸金闕，凡於奏對，備述端由。

translations.literal: Yesterday Guest Reception commissioner Li Yan, sent to Tongliang, lately returned to the golden court; in all his memorial replies he fully set forth the causes.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday Li Yan returned from Tongliang and laid out the whole case at court.

sentences.zh: 其宋光嗣相見之時，於坐上便有言說，先問契丹強弱，次數秦王是非，度此包藏，可見情狀。

translations.literal: When Song Guangsi met him, at table he spoke at once, first asking whether the Khitan were strong or weak, then counting right and wrong for the Prince of Qin—judging this hidden intent, his disposition could be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Song Guangsi at table asked first about Khitan strength, then judged the Prince of Qin—showing his hidden intent.

sentences.zh: 加以疏遠忠直，朋比奸雄。

translations.literal: Moreover he kept the loyal and upright at a distance and befriended treacherous heroes.
translations.idiomatic: He shunned the loyal and clung to villains.

sentences.zh: 內則縱恣輕華，競貪寵位；

translations.literal: Within, he indulged frivolity and competed for favor;
translations.idiomatic: Within, he chased luxury and rank;

sentences.zh: 外則滋彰法令，蠹耗生靈。

translations.literal: without, he multiplied harsh laws and harmed the living.
translations.idiomatic: without, harsh laws drained the people.

sentences.zh: 既德力以不量，在神祇之共憤。

translations.literal: Since his virtue and strength could not be measured, gods and spirits shared in anger.
translations.idiomatic: His power was overreached; heaven and spirits were angered.

sentences.zh: 今命興聖宮使、魏王繼岌充西川四面行營都統，命侍中、樞密使郭崇韜充西川東北面行營都招討製置等使，荊南節度使高季興充西川東南面行營都招討使，鳳翔節度使李嚴充供軍轉運應接等使，同州節度使李令德充行營招討副使，陝府節度使李紹琛充行營蕃漢馬步軍都排陣斬斫使，西京留守張筠充西川管內安撫應接使，華州節度使毛璋充行營左廂馬步都虞候，邠州節度使董璋充行營右廂馬步都虞候，客省使李嚴充西川管內招撫使，總領闕下諸軍，兼西面諸道馬步兵事，取九月十八日進發。

translations.literal: Now Xingsheng Palace commissioner and Prince of Wei Jiji is made overall commander of the four-sided Shu campaign; Palace Attendant and Privy Council commissioner Guo Chongtao is made overall commander and commissioner for the northeast Shu campaign and related matters; Jingnan military commissioner Gao Jixing is made overall commander of the southeast Shu campaign; Fengxiang military commissioner Li Yan is made commissioner for supply transport and support; Tongzhou military commissioner Li Lingde is made campaign deputy commander; Shan prefecture military commissioner Li Shaochen is made overall arraying and cutting commissioner for Han and non-Han horse and foot; western capital regent Zhang Yun is made pacification and support commissioner within Shu; Huazhou military commissioner Mao Zhang is made left wing horse-and-foot chief of the campaign; Binzhou military commissioner Dong Zhang is made right wing horse-and-foot chief; Guest Reception commissioner Li Yan is made pacification commissioner within Shu—commanding all armies below the capital and all western-circuit horse and foot, to advance on the eighteenth day of the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji was made overall Shu commander; Guo Chongtao northeast commander; Gao Jixing southeast commander; Li Yan of Fengxiang supply chief; Li Lingde deputy; Li Shaochen array chief; Zhang Yun pacification chief; Mao Zhang left wing chief; Dong Zhang right wing chief; Li Yan also pacified Shu—leading capital and western forces to march on the eighteenth of the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 凡爾中外，宜體朕懷。

translations.literal: Let all within and without embody Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let the realm heed my intent.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，授魏王繼岌諸道行營都統，餘如故。

translations.literal: On xinchou Prince of Wei Jiji was given overall command of all circuits' campaigns, the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Jiji gained overall command of all circuits; other posts stood.

sentences.zh: 繼岌既受都統之命，以梁漢顒充中軍馬步都虞候兼馬步軍都指揮使，張廷蘊為中軍步軍都指揮使，牛景章充中軍左廂馬軍都指揮使，沈斌充中軍右廂馬軍都指揮使，卓瑰充中軍左廂步軍都指揮使，王贄充中軍右廂步軍都指揮使，供奉官李從襲充中軍馬步軍都監，高品李廷安、呂知柔充魏王衙通謁。

translations.literal: Jiji having received the overall command, Liang Hanyong was made chief of central horse and foot and overall horse-and-foot commander; Zhang Tingyun was central foot commander; Niu Jingzhang was left-wing horse commander; Shen Bin was right-wing horse commander; Zhuo Gui was left-wing foot commander; Wang Zan was right-wing foot commander; Palace Attendant Li Congxi was overall monitor of central horse and foot; senior attendants Li Ting'an and Lü Zhirou were Prince of Wei gate ushers.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji named Liang Hanyong central horse-and-foot chief, Zhang Tingyun foot chief, Niu Jingzhang and Shen Bin wing horse chiefs, Zhuo Gui and Wang Zan wing foot chiefs, Li Congxi monitor, and Li Ting'an and Lü Zhirou ushers.

sentences.zh: 詔工部尚書任圜、翰林學士李愚參魏王軍事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Works Ren Yuan and Hanlin academician Li Yu to join the Prince of Wei's military council.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuan of Works and Hanlin Li Yu joined Jiji's staff.

sentences.zh: 丁未夕，偏天陰雲，北方有聲如雷，野雉皆鳴，俗所謂「天狗落」。

translations.literal: On dingwei at evening the sky was overcast; in the north a sound like thunder; wild pheasants all cried—what common people call "heaven dog falling."
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei at dusk clouds covered the sky; the north thundered and pheasants cried—the folk omen called "heaven dog falling."

sentences.zh: 戊申，魏王繼岌、樞密使侍中郭崇韜進發西征。

translations.literal: On wushen Prince of Wei Jiji and Privy Council commissioner and Palace Attendant Guo Chongtao advanced west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Jiji and Guo Chongtao marched west.

sentences.zh: 太子少師致仕薛廷珪卒，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: Retired Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent Xue Tinggui died and was posthumously made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Retired Junior Mentor Xue Tinggui died and was posthumously Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，幸壽安陵。

translations.literal: On jiayin he visited Shou'an tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he visited Shou'an tomb.

sentences.zh: 司天上言：「自七月三日大雨，至九月十八日後方晴，三辰行度不見。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy reported: "From the third day of the seventh month great rain fell; only after the eighteenth day of the ninth month did it clear—the three luminaries' courses were not seen."
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy reported rain from the third of the seventh until the eighteenth of the ninth hid the stars."

sentences.zh: 」丁巳，幸尖山射雁。

translations.literal: " On dingsi he visited Jianshan to shoot geese.
translations.idiomatic: " On dingsi he hunted geese at Jianshan.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚申朔，宰臣及文武三品以上官赴長壽宮，上大行皇太后諡曰貞簡皇太后。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, gengshen new moon: chief ministers and civil and military officials of the third rank and above went to Changshou Palace and presented the late Empress Dowager's posthumous title as Empress Dowager Zhenjian.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen new moon of the tenth month ministers and officials of the third rank and above named the dowager Empress Zhenjian at Changshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，幸甘泉，遂幸壽安陵。

translations.literal: On xinyou he visited Ganquan, then visited Shou'an tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he visited Ganquan, then Shou'an tomb.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，魏王繼岌率師至鳳翔，先遣使馳檄以諭蜀部。

translations.literal: On renxu Prince of Wei Jiji led the army to Fengxiang and first sent envoys with a flying proclamation to instruct the Shu command.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Jiji reached Fengxiang and sent a swift proclamation to Shu.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，奉皇太后尊諡寶冊赴西京錄座，宰臣豆盧革攝太尉讀冊文，吏部尚書李琪讀寶文，百官素服，班於長壽宮門外奉慰。

translations.literal: On dingmao the honored posthumous patent and treasure were sent to the western capital spirit seat; chief minister Dou Luge acted as Grand Marshal and read the patent; Minister of Personnel Li Qi read the treasure text; the hundred officials in plain robes formed ranks outside Changshou Palace gate to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the dowager's patent and treasure went to the western capital spirit seat; Dou Luge as acting Grand Marshal read the patent, Li Qi the treasure text, and officials in white lined outside Changshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 淮南楊溥遣使進慰禮。

translations.literal: Huainan's Yang Pu sent envoys with condolence gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pu of Huainan sent condolence envoys.

sentences.zh: 己巳，中書上言：「貞簡太后陵請以坤陵為名。

translations.literal: On wusi the Secretariat memorialized: "We ask that Empress Dowager Zhenjian's tomb be named Kunling."
translations.idiomatic: On wusi the Secretariat asked to name the dowager's tomb Kunling.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 初卜山陵，帝欲祔於代州武皇陵，奏議：「天子以四海為家，不當分其南北。

translations.literal: When the tomb site was first divined, the Emperor wished to bury her beside the Martial Emperor's tomb at Daizhou; memorial debate said: "The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home and should not divide north and south.
translations.idiomatic: At first Cunxu wanted her beside Li Keyong's tomb at Daizhou; debate said the Son of Heaven should not split his home north and south.

sentences.zh: 」乃於壽安縣界別卜是陵。

translations.literal: " Then at the Shou'an county border a separate site was divined for this tomb.
translations.idiomatic: " So a separate site was chosen on the Shou'an border.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》載中書門下奏議云：「人君以四海為家，不當分其南北。

translations.literal: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》 records a Secretariat and Chancellery memorial: "The ruler takes the four seas as home and should not divide north and south.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》 cites a Secretariat memorial: "The ruler's home is the four seas, not north against south.

sentences.zh: 洛陽是帝王之宅，四時朝拜，禮須便近，不能遠幸代州。

translations.literal: Luoyang is the imperial dwelling; seasonal audiences require convenient proximity and cannot rely on distant travel to Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang is the imperial seat; seasonal rites need nearness, not distant Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 今漢朝諸陵，皆近秦雍，國朝陵寢，布列京畿。

translations.literal: Now the Han dynasty's tombs all lie near Qin and Yong; our dynasty's imperial tombs are spread through the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Han tombs cluster near Qin and Yong; Tang imperial tombs lie around the capital.

sentences.zh: 後魏文帝自代遷洛之後，園陵皆在河南，兼敕功臣之家，不許北葬，今魏氏諸陵尚在京畿。

translations.literal: After Northern Wei Wendi moved from Dai to Luo, park-tombs were all in Henan, and meritorious households were forbidden northern burial; Wei clan tombs still lie in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Wendi left Dai for Luo, tombs stayed in Henan and meritorious houses could not bury north; Wei tombs still stand near the capital.

sentences.zh: 祔葬代州，理未為允。

translations.literal: Burial beside Daizhou is not reasonable in principle."
translations.idiomatic: Burial at Daizhou is not reasonable."

translations.literal: " It was approved.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.)〉

sentences.zh: 丙子，以前翰林學士、戶部侍郎馮道依前本官充職。

translations.literal: On bingzi former Hanlin academician and Minister of Revenue Feng Dao was confirmed in his former office and post.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Feng Dao kept his former Hanlin and Revenue posts.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，西征之師入大散關，

translations.literal: On wuyin, the western campaign army entered Great Scatter Pass,
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the western campaign force entered Great Scatter Pass,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·趙廷隱傳》云：自入敵境，即禁兵士焚廬舍，剽財物，蜀人德之。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Nine States Institutes · Zhao Tingyin Biography》 says: from entering enemy territory they forbade soldiers to burn houses or plunder goods, and the Shu people were grateful.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine States Institutes · Zhao Tingyin》 says that on entering Shu they forbade burning homes or looting, and the people were grateful.)〉

sentences.zh: 偽命鳳州節度使王承捷、故鎮屯駐指揮使唐景思次第迎降，得兵一萬二千、軍儲四十萬。

translations.literal: The Shu-appointed Fengzhou military commissioner Wang Chengjie and the former garrison commander Tang Jingsi in succession came to surrender; they gained twelve thousand troops and four hundred thousand in military stores.
translations.idiomatic: Shu-appointed Fengzhou commissioner Wang Chengjie and former garrison commander Tang Jingsi surrendered in turn, yielding twelve thousand men and four hundred thousand in stores.

sentences.zh: 又下三泉，得軍儲三十餘萬。

translations.literal: They also took Sanquan and gained more than three hundred thousand in military stores.
translations.idiomatic: They also took Sanquan and gained over three hundred thousand in stores.

sentences.zh: 自是師無匱乏，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: From then on the army lacked nothing and its renown greatly swelled.
translations.idiomatic: From then the army wanted for nothing and its fame soared.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，偽興州刺史王承鑒、成州刺史王承樸棄城遁去，康延孝大破蜀軍於三泉。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Shu Xingzhou prefect Wang Chengjian and Chengzhou prefect Wang Chengpu abandoned their cities and fled; Kang Yanxiao routed the Shu army at Sanquan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the Shu Xingzhou prefect Wang Chengjian and Chengzhou prefect Wang Chengpu fled their cities, and Kang Yanxiao crushed the Shu army at Sanquan.

sentences.zh: 時王衍將幸秦州，以其軍五萬屯於利州。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Yan was about to visit Qinzhou and stationed his fifty-thousand-man army at Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was then bound for Qinzhou with fifty thousand men at Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 聞我師至，遣步騎三萬逆戰於三泉，延孝與李嚴以勁騎三千擊之，蜀軍大敗，斬首五千級，餘眾奔潰。

translations.literal: Hearing our army had come, he sent thirty thousand foot and horse to meet battle at Sanquan; Yanxiao and Li Yan with three thousand crack cavalry struck them, the Shu army was greatly defeated, five thousand heads were taken, and the rest scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of our approach he sent thirty thousand foot and horse to Sanquan; Yanxiao and Li Yan with three thousand picked cavalry routed them, took five thousand heads, and drove the rest to flight.

sentences.zh: 王衍聞敗，自利州奔歸成都，斷吉柏津，浮梁而去。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, hearing of defeat, fled from Lizhou back to Chengdu, cut the Jibo Ford, and crossed on a pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan fled Lizhou for Chengdu, severed the Jibo crossing, and escaped on a pontoon bridge.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，文武百官上表，以貞簡皇太后靈駕發引，請車駕不至山陵所。

translations.literal: On dinghai, civil and military officials jointly memorialized that with the spirit carriage of Empress Dowager Zhenjian setting out, they asked that the imperial carriage not go to the mausoleum precinct.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the civil and military ranks asked that with Empress Dowager Zhenjian's spirit carriage setting out Cunxu not go to the tomb precinct.

sentences.zh: 戊子，葬貞簡太后於坤陵。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Empress Dowager Zhenjian was buried at Kun Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Empress Dowager Zhenjian was buried at Kun Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 己丑，魏王繼岌至興州，偽東川節度使宋光葆以梓、綿、劍、龍、普五州來降；

translations.literal: On jichou, the Prince of Wei Jiji reached Xingzhou; Shu Dongchuan military commissioner Song Guangbao surrendered Zi, Mian, Jian, Long, and Pu prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Prince of Wei Jiji reached Xing; Shu Dongchuan commissioner Song Guangbao surrendered Zi, Mian, Jian, Long, and Pu;

sentences.zh: 武定軍使王承肇以達、蓬、璧三州來降；

translations.literal: Wuding army commissioner Wang Chengzhao surrendered Da, Peng, and Bi prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Wuding commissioner Wang Chengzhao surrendered Da, Peng, and Bi;

sentences.zh: 興元節度使王宗威以梁、開、通、渠、麟五州來降；

translations.literal: Xingyuan military commissioner Wang Zongwei surrendered Liang, Kai, Tong, Qu, and Lin prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan commissioner Wang Zongwei surrendered Liang, Kai, Tong, Qu, and Lin;

sentences.zh: 階州刺史王承嶽納符印請命；

translations.literal: Jiezhou prefect Wang Chengyue submitted his tally and seal to request orders;
translations.idiomatic: Jie prefect Wang Chengyue handed over his seal and asked for orders;

sentences.zh: 秦州節度使王承休棄城自扶路奔於西川。

translations.literal: Qinzhou military commissioner Wang Chengxu abandoned the city and fled by the Fulu road into western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Qin commissioner Wang Chengxu abandoned his city and fled by the Fulu road into Shu.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《太平廣記》引《王氏見聞記》云：王承休握銳兵於天水，兵刃不舉。

translations.literal: (The 《Extensive Records》 cites the 《Wang Clan Seen and Heard》: Wang Chengxu held crack troops at Tianshui yet would not raise weapons.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Extensive Records》 cites the 《Wang Clan Seen and Heard》: Wang Chengxu held elite troops at Tianshui yet never fought.

sentences.zh: 既知東軍入蜀，遂擁麾下之師及婦女孩幼萬餘口、金銀繒帛，於西蕃買路歸蜀。

translations.literal: Once he knew the eastern army had entered Shu, he led his troops and more than ten thousand wives, children, girls, and young, with gold, silk, and brocade, and bought a road through the western tribes back to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the eastern army had entered Shu, he marched his command and more than ten thousand women and children with gold and silk to buy passage through the western tribes.

sentences.zh: 沿路為西蕃擄奪，凍餓相踐而死，迨至蜀，存者百餘人，唯與田宗汭等脫身而至。

translations.literal: Along the way western tribes plundered them; freezing and hunger trampled one another to death; by the time they reached Shu barely more than a hundred survived, and only he with Tian Zongmin and a few others escaped through alive.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes along the road plundered them; cold and hunger killed multitudes; barely a hundred reached Shu, and only he, Tian Zongmin, and a few others got through.

sentences.zh: 魏王使人問之曰：「親握重兵，何得不戰？

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei sent someone to ask him: "Holding heavy forces in your own hand, why did you not fight?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wei's envoy asked, "You held a great army—why not fight?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「畏大王神武，不敢當其鋒。

translations.literal: He said: "I feared the great prince's divine martial prowess and dared not meet his edge."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I feared Your Highness's might and dared not meet your edge."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「何不早降？

translations.literal: They said: "Why not surrender early?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy asked, "Why not surrender sooner?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「蓋緣王師不入封部，無門納款。

translations.literal: He said: "It was because the royal army had not entered my circuit; there was no gate to offer allegiance."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The royal army had not entered my circuit; I had no way to submit."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「初入蕃部幾許人？

translations.literal: They said: "How many entered the foreign lands at first?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy asked, "How many entered the tribes at first?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「 萬餘口。

translations.literal: He said: "More than ten thousand mouths."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "More than ten thousand mouths."

sentences.zh: 」「今存者幾何？

translations.literal: "How many survive now?"
translations.idiomatic: "How many survive now?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「才及百數。

translations.literal: He said: "Only about a hundred."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Only about a hundred."

sentences.zh: 」魏王曰：「汝可償萬人之命。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei said: "You can pay for ten thousand lives."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wei said, "You owe ten thousand lives."

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。）〉

translations.literal: Then he was beheaded.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He was beheaded.)〉

sentences.zh: 十一月庚寅朔，帝幸壽安，號慟於坤陵。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, gengyin new moon: the Emperor visited Shou'an and wailed at Kun Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin new moon of the eleventh month Cunxu visited Shou'an and wailed at Kun Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以振武節度使朱守殷為兗州節度使。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Zhenwu military commissioner Zhu Shouyin was made Yanzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Zhu Shouyin of Zhenwu became Yan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 徐州、鄴都上言，十月二十五日夜，地大震。

translations.literal: Xuzhou and Yedu memorialized that on the night of the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month the earth greatly quaked.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Yedu reported a great earthquake on the night of the twenty-fifth of the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 康延孝至利州，修吉柏津浮梁。

translations.literal: Kang Yanxiao reached Lizhou and repaired the Jibo Ford pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yanxiao reached Lizhou and rebuilt the Jibo pontoon bridge.

sentences.zh: 偽昭武軍節度使林思諤來降。

translations.literal: The Shu Zhaowu army military commissioner Lin Si'e came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Zhaowu commissioner Lin Si'e surrendered.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，魏王過利州，帝賜王衍詔，諭以禍福。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Prince of Wei passed Lizhou; the Emperor bestowed an edict on Wang Yan, instructing him on fortune and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the Prince of Wei passed Lizhou; Cunxu sent Wang Yan an edict on fortune and ruin.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏王至劍州，偽武信軍節度使王宗壽以遂、合、渝、瀘、忠五州來降。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Prince of Wei reached Jianzhou; Shu Wuxin army military commissioner Wang Zongshou surrendered Sui, He, Yu, Lu, and Zhong prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Prince of Wei reached Jian; the Shu Wuxin commissioner Wang Zongshou surrendered Sui, He, Yu, Lu, and Zhong.

sentences.zh: 丁未，高麗國遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Goryeo state sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Goryeo sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 康延孝、李嚴至漢州，王衍遣人送牛酒請降，李嚴遂先入成都。

translations.literal: Kang Yanxiao and Li Yan reached Hanzhou; Wang Yan sent men with oxen and wine to request surrender, and Li Yan thereupon first entered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yanxiao and Li Yan reached Han; Wang Yan sent oxen and wine to sue for surrender, and Li Yan entered Chengdu first.

sentences.zh: 戊申，祔貞簡皇太后神主於太廟。

translations.literal: On wushen, Empress Dowager Zhenjian's spirit tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Empress Dowager Zhenjian's tablet was placed in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 己酉，魏王至綿州，王衍遣使上箋歸命。

translations.literal: On jiyou, the Prince of Wei reached Mianzhou; Wang Yan sent envoys with a written submission to offer allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou the Prince of Wei reached Mian; Wang Yan sent envoys with a written submission of allegiance.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，皇弟鄆州節度使存霸、滑州節度使存渥、左金吾大將軍晉州節度使存乂、邢州節度使存紀，並授起復雲麾將軍、右金吾大將軍同正。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Emperor's younger brother Yanzhou military commissioner Cunba, Hua prefecture military commissioner Cunwo, Left Golden Spear Guard senior general and Jinzhou military commissioner Cunyi, and Xingzhou military commissioner Cunji were all appointed recalled-from-mourning Cloud Banner generals and Right Golden Spear Guard senior generals of the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Cunba of Yan, Cunwo of Hua, Cunyi of Jin as Left Golden Spear senior general, and Cunji of Xing were all recalled from mourning as Cloud Banner generals and Right Golden Spear senior generals of the same rank.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使高季興奏，收復歸、夔、忠等州。

translations.literal: Jingnan military commissioner Gao Jixing memorialized that he had recovered Gui, Qi, and Zhong prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan commissioner Gao Jixing reported recovering Gui, Qi, and Zhong.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魏王至德陽。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Prince of Wei reached Deyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the Prince of Wei reached Deyang.

sentences.zh: 偽六軍使王宗弼報，王衍舉家遷於西宅，宗弼權稱西川兵馬留後；

translations.literal: The Shu Six Armies commissioner Wang Zongbi reported that Wang Yan had moved his whole household to the western residence and Zongbi provisionally styled himself western Shu army-and-horse retention commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Six Armies commissioner Wang Zongbi reported that Wang Yan had moved his household to the western residence and Zongbi styled himself acting western Shu army retention commissioner;

sentences.zh: 又報偽樞密使宋光嗣景潤澄、宣徽使李周輅歐陽晃同有異謀，惑亂蜀主，已梟斬訖。

translations.literal: he also reported that Shu privy commissioners Song Guangsi, Jing Runcheng, and Director of the Palace Secretariat Li Zhou, Ouyang Huang, and others alike harbored divergent plots, confused the Shu ruler, and had already been beheaded and displayed.
translations.idiomatic: he also reported that Shu privy commissioners Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng, Secretariat director Li Zhou, Ouyang Huang, and others had plotted against the ruler and were already beheaded and displayed.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·王宗弼傳》：唐師陷鳳州，衍遣三招討屯三泉以拒唐師，未戰，三招討俱遁走，因令宗弼守綿穀而誅三招討，宗弼遂與三招討同送款於魏王。

translations.literal: (The 《Nine States Institutes · Wang Zongbi Biography》: when Tang troops took Fengzhou, Yan dispatched the three campaign commanders to camp at Sanquan to resist Tang; before battle all three campaign commanders fled; he then ordered Zongbi to hold Mian Valley and executed the three campaign commanders; Zongbi thereupon with the three campaign commanders together sent allegiance to the Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine States Institutes · Wang Zongbi》 says when Tang took Feng, Yan sent three campaign commanders to Sanquan; before battle all three fled; Yan ordered Zongbi to hold Mian Valley and killed the three commanders; Zongbi then with them submitted to the Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 乃還成都，斬宋光嗣等，函首送於魏王，遷衍及母妻於西宮。）〉

translations.literal: He then returned to Chengdu, beheaded Song Guangsi and the rest, sent their heads in boxes to the Prince of Wei, and moved Yan and his mother and wife to the western palace.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Chengdu, killed Song Guangsi and the rest, sent their heads to the Prince of Wei, and moved Yan, his mother, and his wife to the western palace.)〉

sentences.zh: 壬子，王衍遣使上表請降。

translations.literal: On renzi, Wang Yan sent envoys with a memorial requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Wang Yan sent envoys with a surrender memorial.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以吳越國馬步統軍使、檢校太傅錢元球為檢校太尉、守侍中，充靜海軍節度使。

translations.literal: On guichou, Wuyue state horse-and-foot overall commander and acting Grand Tutor Qian Yuanqiu was made acting Grand Preceptor, Palace Attendant, and Jinghai army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Qian Yuanqiu of Wuyue—horse-and-foot overall commander and acting Grand Tutor—became acting Grand Preceptor, palace attendant, and Jinghai commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，魏王至西川城北。

translations.literal: On yimao, the Prince of Wei reached the north of western Shu's capital city.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the Prince of Wei reached the north wall of the Shu capital.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，蜀主王衍出降，語在衍傳。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Shu ruler Wang Yan came out to surrender—the account is in the Yan biography.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Shu ruler Wang Yan surrendered—the account is in his biography.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，大軍入成都，法令嚴峻，市不易肆。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the great army entered Chengdu; laws and orders were stern, and the markets did not change their stalls.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the main army entered Chengdu under strict law, and the markets stayed open as before.

sentences.zh: 自興師凡七十五日，蜀平，得兵士三萬、兵仗七百萬、糧三百五十三萬、錢一百九十二萬貫、金銀共二十二萬兩、珠玉犀象二萬、紋錦綾羅五十萬，得節度州十、郡六十四、縣二百四十九。

translations.literal: From raising the army it was seventy-five days; Shu was pacified. They gained thirty thousand soldiers, seven million weapons, three million five hundred thirty thousand in grain, one million nine hundred twenty thousand strings of cash, gold and silver totaling two hundred twenty thousand liang, pearls, jade, rhinoceros horn, and ivory twenty thousand, patterned brocade and damask five hundred thousand, ten military commission prefectures, sixty-four commanderies, and two hundred forty-nine counties.
translations.idiomatic: In seventy-five days from mobilization Shu fell: thirty thousand troops, seven million weapons, 3.53 million in grain, 1.92 million strings of cash, 220,000 liang of gold and silver, 20,000 of pearls, jade, rhinoceros, and ivory, 500,000 of brocade, ten commission prefectures, sixty-four commanderies, and 249 counties.

sentences.zh: 己丑，禮儀使奏：「貞簡皇太后升祔禮畢，一應宗廟伎樂及諸祀並請仍舊。

translations.literal: On jichou, the commissioner of rites memorialized: "The rites of elevating Empress Dowager Zhenjian's spirit tablet to the temple are complete; all ancestral temple musicians and the various sacrifices should remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the rites commissioner reported, "With Empress Dowager Zhenjian enshrined, ancestral musicians and all sacrifices should stay as before.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: 」The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬戌，以前雲州節度使李存敬為同州節度使；

translations.literal: Twelfth month, renxu: former Yunzhou military commissioner Li Cunjing was made Tongzhou military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month on renxu former Yun commissioner Li Cunjing became Tong commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以同州節度使、檢校太保、同平章事李令德為遂州節度使；

translations.literal: Tongzhou military commissioner, acting Grand Guardian, and co-equal chief minister Li Lingde was made Suizhou military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingde of Tong—acting Grand Guardian and chancellor—became Sui commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以邠州節度使、檢校太保董璋為劍南東川節度副大使、知節度事；

translations.literal: Binzhou military commissioner and acting Grand Guardian Dong Zhang was made Jiannan Dongchuan military vice commissioner and acting commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang of Bin—acting Grand Guardian—became Jiannan Dongchuan vice commissioner and acting commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以華州節度使毛璋為邠州節度使；

translations.literal: Hua prefecture military commissioner Mao Zhang was made Binzhou military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zhang of Hua became Bin commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以左金吾大將軍史敬熔為華州節度使。

translations.literal: Left Golden Spear Guard senior general Shi Jingrong was made Hua prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingrong of the Left Golden Spear Guard became Hua commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以武寧軍節度副使李紹文為兗州觀察留後。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Wuning army vice commissioner Li Shaowen was made Yanzhou observation retention commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Li Shaowen, Wuning vice commissioner, became Yan observation retention commissioner.

sentences.zh: 庚午，宴諸王武臣於長春殿，始用樂。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the princes and martial officials were feasted at Everlasting Spring Hall; music was used for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Cunxu feasted princes and martial officers at Everlasting Spring Hall and used music for the first time.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以北京副留守、太原尹孟知祥為檢校太傅、同平章事、成都尹、劍南西川節度副大使、知節度事、西山八國雲南都招撫等使；

translations.literal: On bingzi, northern capital deputy regent and Taiyuan prefect Meng Zhixiang was made acting Grand Tutor, co-equal chief minister, Chengdu prefect, Jiannan Xichuan military vice commissioner, acting commissioner, and commissioner for pacification of the western mountains' eight states and Yunnan and the rest;
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Meng Zhixiang—northern deputy regent and Taiyuan prefect—became acting Grand Tutor, chancellor, Chengdu prefect, Jiannan Xichuan vice commissioner and acting commissioner, and pacification commissioner for the western mountains and Yunnan;

sentences.zh: 以戶部尚書王正言為檢校吏部尚書、守興唐尹，充鄴都副留守；

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Wang Zhengyan was made acting Minister of Personnel, acting Xingtang prefect, and Yedu deputy regent;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengyan of Revenue became acting Personnel minister, acting Xingtang prefect, and Yedu deputy regent;

sentences.zh: 以鄴都副留守、興唐尹張憲檢校吏部尚書、太原尹，充北京副留守、知留守事。

translations.literal: Yedu deputy regent and Xingtang prefect Zhang Xian was made acting Minister of Personnel, Taiyuan prefect, and northern capital deputy regent with charge of regency affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian—Yedu deputy regent and Xingtang prefect—became acting Personnel minister, Taiyuan prefect, and northern deputy regent in charge of regency.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以臘辰狩於白沙，皇后、皇子、宮人畢從。

translations.literal: On jimao, on the La festival day he hunted at White Sand; the empress, imperial sons, and palace women all followed.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, the La festival, Cunxu hunted at White Sand with the empress, princes, and palace women in attendance.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，次伊闕。

translations.literal: On gengchen, he halted at Yique.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he camped at Yique.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，次潭泊。

translations.literal: On xinsi, he halted at Tan Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi he camped at Tan Marsh.

sentences.zh: 壬午，次龕澗。

translations.literal: On renwu, he halted at Kan Ravine.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu he camped at Kan Ravine.

sentences.zh: 癸未，還宮。

translations.literal: On guiwei, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是時大雪苦寒，吏士有凍踣於路者。

translations.literal: At that time great snow and bitter cold; officers and soldiers froze and fell on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Great snow and bitter cold then; men froze and fell along the roads.

sentences.zh: 伊、汝之民，饑乏尤甚，衛兵所至，責其供餉，既不能給，因壞其什器，撤其廬舍而焚之，甚於剽劫。

translations.literal: The people of Yi and Ru were especially short of food; wherever the guard troops arrived they demanded provisions; when they could not supply them the troops smashed their utensils, tore down their huts and burned them—worse than bandit raids.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Ru were starving worst; guards demanded rations, and when villagers could not pay they smashed goods, tore down huts, and burned them—worse than raiders.

sentences.zh: 縣吏畏恐，竄避於山谷間。

translations.literal: County clerks in fear hid in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: County clerks fled in fear to mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 甲申，出御劄示中書門下，以今歲水災異常，所在人戶流徙，以避征賦，關市之征，抽納繁碎，宜令宰臣商量條奏。

translations.literal: On jiashen, an imperial note was issued to the Secretariat and Chancellery: because this year's floods were abnormal, households everywhere were drifting away to escape levies, and market tolls and exactions were drawn in tangled detail—let the chief ministers deliberate and memorialize articles.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Cunxu showed the Secretariat a note: floods had driven people off to escape taxes and market tolls were crushing—he asked the chancellors to draft remedies.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，第三姑宋氏封義寧大長公主，長姊孟氏封瓊華長公主，第十一妹張氏封瑤英長公主。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the third aunt the Song clan was enfeoffed Princess of Great Righteousness and Tranquility; the elder sister the Meng clan Princess of Jade Splendor; the eleventh younger sister the Zhang clan Princess of Jade Blossom.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu third aunt Song was made Princess of Great Righteousness and Tranquility, elder sister Meng Princess of Jade Splendor, and eleventh sister Zhang Princess of Jade Blossom.

sentences.zh: 閏十二月甲午，賜中書門下詔曰：

translations.literal: Intercalary twelfth month, jiawu: an edict was bestowed on the Secretariat and Chancellery, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary twelfth month on jiawu an edict to the Secretariat said:

sentences.zh: 朕聞古先哲王，臨御天下，上則以無偏無黨為至治，次則以足食足兵為遠謀，緬惟前修，誠可師範。

translations.literal: We have heard that the ancient sage kings, in ruling All-under-Heaven, took above all being without bias and without cliques as the utmost governance, and next took full food and full arms as far-reaching design—the former worthies may truly be taken as models.
translations.idiomatic: We hear that ancient sage kings ruled by being without bias or cliques above all, and next by full bellies and full arsenals—worthies we may truly follow.

sentences.zh: 朕纂承鳳曆，嗣守鴻圖，三載於茲，萬機是總，非不知五兵未弭，兆庶多艱，蓋賴卿等寅亮居懷，康濟為務，冀盡數輿之理，洞詢盍徹之規。

translations.literal: We have inherited the imperial succession and guarded the great design; three years to now the myriad affairs are all summarized—not that we do not know the five weapons are not laid down and the myriad people face many hardships, but we rely on you to be reverently bright in purpose and take relief as your task, hoping to exhaust the reason of the carriage and thoroughly inquire into the rule of clearing away.
translations.idiomatic: We have inherited the throne and held the reins three years—not unaware that arms are not stilled and the people suffer, but trusting you to be reverent and take relief as your charge, hoping to exhaust policy and clear every abuse.

sentences.zh: 今則潛按方區，備聆謠俗，或力役罕均其勞逸，或賦租莫辨於後先，但以督促為名，煩苛不已。

translations.literal: Now we have secretly examined the regions and fully heard village songs: sometimes corvée was rarely equal in toil and rest, sometimes tax levies could not be distinguished first from last, but they only took urging as their name and harassment never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Now we have quietly examined the regions and heard the villages: corvée was uneven, taxes could not tell first from last, yet officers only urged and harassed without end.

sentences.zh: 被甲胄者何嘗充給，趨朝省者轉困支持，州閭之貨殖全疏，天地之災祥屢應。

translations.literal: Those in armor—when were they ever fully supplied? Those hurrying to court grew weary supporting the capital; the prefectures' wealth was wholly drained; heaven and earth's omens of calamity answered again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Armored men were never fully supplied; men rushing to court were worn supporting the capital; local wealth was drained; omens of disaster answered again and again.

sentences.zh: 以至星辰越度，旱澇不時，農桑失業於丘園，道堇相望於郊野，生靈及此，寢食寧遑，豈非朕德政未孚，焦勞自拙者耶！

translations.literal: So that the stars crossed their degrees, drought and flood were untimely, farming and sericulture failed in hamlet and garden, corpses on the roads looked across the suburbs—is it not that our virtuous government has not won trust and our anxious toil has been our own clumsiness!
translations.idiomatic: Stars crossed their stations, drought and flood came untimely, farms failed, corpses lined the suburbs—is it not that our government has not won trust and our anxious toil has been clumsiness!

sentences.zh: 朕昨親援毫翰，軫念瘡痍，一則詢爾謀猷，一則表予宵旰，未披來奏，轉撓於懷，敢不翼翼罪躬，乾乾軫慮。

translations.literal: Yesterday we personally took up the brush and thought of the wounded; on the one hand we inquired of your counsels, on the other we showed our sleeplessness—before your memorial came it still troubled our breast; how dare we not tread carefully in guilt and work diligently in care.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday we took up the brush for the wounded, asked your counsel, and showed our sleeplessness—before your answer came it still troubled us; how dare we not tread carefully in guilt and work hard in care.

sentences.zh: 谘爾四嶽，弼予一人，何不舉賢才，裨寡昧。

translations.literal: We consult you, the Four Peaks, to assist us alone—why not raise worthy talent to aid our dimness.
translations.idiomatic: We consult you, the Four Peaks, to assist us—why not raise worthy talent to aid our dimness.

sentences.zh: 百辟之內，群後之間，莫不有盡忠者被掩其能，抱器者艱陳其力。

translations.literal: Within the hundred offices, among the host of lords, is there not one who gave full loyalty yet had his ability masked, or bore talent yet found it hard to state his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Among the hundred offices and host of lords, has not the fully loyal had his ability masked, and the talented found it hard to speak?

sentences.zh: 或草澤有遺逸之士，山林多屈滯之人，爾所不知，吾將安訪！

translations.literal: Perhaps in grass and marshes there are scholars the court missed, in mountains and forests many men stuck in low rank—what you do not know, how shall we inquire!
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps grass and marsh hide scholars the court missed, mountains and forests men stuck in rank—what you do not know, how shall we inquire!

sentences.zh: 卿等位尊調鼎，名顯代天，既逢不諱之朝，何吝由衷之說，當宜曆告中外，急訪英髦。

translations.literal: You stand high tuning the cauldron, your names shine representing Heaven; having met a court without taboo, why be sparing of heartfelt speech—at once you should tell it throughout inner and outer, and urgently seek outstanding men.
translations.idiomatic: You stand high tuning the cauldron, your names shine for Heaven; in a court without taboo, why spare heartfelt speech—tell it throughout the realm and urgently seek outstanding men.

sentences.zh: 應在仕及前資文武官已下，至草澤之士，有濟國治民、除奸革弊者，並宜各獻封章，朕當選擇施行。

translations.literal: Whether currently in office or former civil and military officials down to grass-and-marsh scholars, whoever can aid the state and govern the people or remove traitors and reform abuses—all should each submit sealed memorials; we shall select and carry out.
translations.idiomatic: Whether in office or former civil and military ranks down to grass-and-marsh scholars, whoever can aid the state, govern the people, or remove traitors and reform abuses should submit sealed memorials; we shall select and enact.

sentences.zh: 其近宣御劄，亦告諭內外，體朕意焉。

translations.literal: The recent imperial note should also be proclaimed within and without to embody our intent.
translations.idiomatic: The recent imperial note should also be proclaimed within and without to embody our intent.

sentences.zh: 是時，兩河大水，戶口流亡者十四五，都下供饋不充，軍士乏食，乃有鬻子去妻，老弱采拾於野，殍踣於行路者。

translations.literal: At that time the two He regions had great floods; fourteen or fifteen in ten of the population were refugees; supplies for the capital were not sufficient and the soldiers lacked food—there were those who sold children and put away wives, the old and weak gathering gleanings in the wild and falling dead on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Then the two He regions flooded; fourteen or fifteen in ten fled; the capital went short and soldiers starved—some sold children and put away wives, the old gleaned in the wild and died on the roads.

sentences.zh: 州郡飛挽，旋給京師，租庸使孔謙日於上東門外佇望其來，算而給之。

translations.literal: The prefectures rushed transport in rotation to supply the capital; rent-and-corvée commissioner Kong Qian daily waited outside the upper east gate for its arrival, calculated it, and issued it.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures rushed grain in turn to the capital; rent-and-corvée commissioner Kong Qian daily waited at the upper east gate to tally and issue it.

sentences.zh: 加以所在泥潦，輦運艱難，愁歎之聲，盈於道路，四方地震，天象乖越。

translations.literal: Moreover everywhere was mud and flood; cart transport was hard; sounds of grief filled the roads; earthquakes struck the four quarters; heavenly signs were aberrant.
translations.idiomatic: Mud and flood everywhere made carting hard; grief filled the roads; earthquakes struck the four quarters; the heavens were aberrant.

sentences.zh: 帝深憂之，問所司濟贍之術。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply troubled and asked the responsible offices for methods to relieve and support.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu was deeply troubled and asked the offices for relief.

sentences.zh: 孔謙比以吏進，故無保邦濟民之要務，唯以急刻賦斂為事。

translations.literal: Kong Qian had lately advanced through clerical service, so he had no essentials of securing the state and aiding the people—he only took urgent harsh levies as his business.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian had lately risen through clerks, so he knew no way to secure the state—he only made harsh levies his business.

sentences.zh: 樞密承旨段徊奏曰：「臣見本朝時或遇歲時災歉，國費不足，天子將求經濟之要，則內出朱書御劄，以訪宰臣，請陛下依此故事行之。

translations.literal: Privy Council bearer Duan Huai memorialized: "Your servant sees that in our dynasty whenever there were yearly disasters and state expenses were insufficient, the Son of Heaven would seek the essentials of managing the economy and take out from within a vermilion-written imperial note to inquire of the chief ministers—we ask Your Majesty to follow this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Privy bearer Duan Huai reported, "In our dynasty when famine emptied the treasury the Son of Heaven would take out a vermilion imperial note to ask the chancellors—we ask Your Majesty to follow that precedent.

sentences.zh: 」即命學士草詞，帝親劄以訪宰臣，非帝憂民之實也。

translations.literal: 」At once academicians were ordered to draft the wording; the Emperor personally wrote a note to inquire of the chief ministers—it was not the Emperor's real concern for the people.
translations.idiomatic: 」Academicians were ordered to draft words; Cunxu personally wrote a note to the chancellors—it was not real concern for the people.

sentences.zh: 時宰相豆盧革等依阿徇旨，竟無所陳，但云：「陛下威德冠天下，今西蜀平定，珍寶甚多，可以給軍。

translations.literal: At that time chief ministers Dou Luge and the rest fawned on the intent and ultimately offered nothing, only saying: "Your Majesty's martial virtue crowns All-under-Heaven; now western Shu is pacified and treasures are very many—they can supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Then chancellors Dou Luge and the rest fawned and offered nothing, only saying, "Your Majesty's might crowns the realm; western Shu is pacified and treasures abound—they can feed the army.

sentences.zh: 水旱作沴，天之常道，不足以貽聖憂。

translations.literal: Flood and drought as calamity are heaven's constant way and are not enough to burden sage worry.
translations.idiomatic: Flood and drought are heaven's constant way and not enough to burden sage worry.

sentences.zh: 」中官李紹宏奏曰：「俟魏王旋軍之後，若兵額漸多，饋挽難給，請且幸汴州，以便漕挽。

translations.literal: 」The inner eunuch Li Shaohong memorialized: "When the Prince of Wei returns from the army, if troop quotas gradually increase, transport supply will be hard to provide—please for the present move the court to Bianzhou to facilitate canal transport."
translations.idiomatic: 」Eunuch Li Shaohong said, "After the Prince of Wei returns, larger armies will strain supply—move the court temporarily to Bianzhou for easier canal grain."

sentences.zh: 」時群臣獻議者亦多，大較詞理迂闊，不中時病。

translations.literal: 」At the time many among the court ministers also offered proposals; on the whole their reasoning was circuitous and wide of the mark and did not hit the illnesses of the time.
translations.idiomatic: 」Many ministers offered advice too, but most was roundabout and missed the crisis.

sentences.zh: 唯吏部尚書李琪引古田租之法，從權救弊之道，上疏言之，帝優詔以獎之。

translations.literal: Only Minister of Personnel Li Qi cited the ancient field-tax law and a course of saving abuses by expedient authority, submitted a memorial stating it, and the Emperor with a favorable edict rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Qi of Personnel cited ancient land-tax law and flexible relief, memorialized, and the Emperor answered with a gracious edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔偽蜀私署官員等：「惟名與器，不可假人，況是遐僻偏方，僭竊偽署，因時亂而濫稱名位，歸國體而悉合削除。

translations.literal: On dingyou, an edict to the privately appointed officers of false Shu, etc.: "Fame and instruments may not be lent to others; how much more a remote corner and alien region that usurped and stole false appointments—because of the disorder of the time they recklessly claimed ranks and titles; now that they return to the national body, all should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou an edict on Shu's self-appointed officers said, "Titles and offices must not be given away; a remote rebel province that seized ranks in chaos must lose them all on returning to the empire.

sentences.zh: 但恐當本朝屯否之時，有歷代簪纓之士，既陷彼土，遂授偽官。

translations.literal: Yet we fear that when our dynasty was in hardship, there were gentry of successive generations who, having fallen into that land, then received false offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some eminent families, trapped in Shu when the court was in distress, took rebel posts.

sentences.zh: 又慮有曾受本朝渥恩，當時已居班秩，須為升降，不可通同。

translations.literal: We also worry that some once received our dynasty's generous favor and at the time already held court ranks—they require promotion or demotion and may not be treated alike.
translations.idiomatic: Some who already held Tang rank under imperial grace need individual promotion or demotion, not one rule.

sentences.zh: 應偽署官至太師、太傅及三少，並太尉、司徒、司空、侍中、中書令、左右僕射已上，並宜降至六尚書，臨時更約偽署高低為六行次第。

translations.literal: Those who held false appointments as Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and the Three Junior Tutors, as well as Grand Commander, Grand Mentor, Grand Minister, Palace Attendant, Secretariat Director, and Left and Right Vice Directors and above—all should be reduced to the six department ministers; for the moment further match false rank high and low into six grades of precedence.
translations.idiomatic: False Grand Preceptors, tutors, Three Junior Tutors, Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, Secretariat Director, and Vice Directors and above should drop to the six ministries, ranked in six grades by former false rank.

sentences.zh: 階至開府、特進、金紫者，宜令文班降至朝散大夫，武班降至銀青。

translations.literal: Those whose rank reached Opening Office, Special Advancement, or golden fish and purple robe—the civil roster should be reduced to Spread Radiance Grand Master; the military roster to silver seal and blue robe.
translations.idiomatic: Honorary Grand Tutor, Special Advancement, or gold-and-purple ranks fall to Spread Radiance Grand Master in civil posts and silver-seal blue robe in military posts.

sentences.zh: 爵偽署將相已下與開國男，餘並不得更稱封爵，其有功臣者削去。

translations.literal: Noble titles: for false-appointed generals and ministers down to Baron Who Founded a State, the rest may no longer claim enfeoffed titles; those with merit marks should have them stripped.
translations.idiomatic: False generals, ministers, and barons may keep no other noble titles; meritorious titles are also stripped.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》作：其有功臣名號，並宜削去。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 reads: those with meritorious-title designations should also be stripped.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 adds that meritorious-title designations should also be stripped.)〉

sentences.zh: 如是偽署節鎮，伐罪之初，率先向化及立功效者，宜委繼岌、崇韜臨時獎任。

translations.literal: As for false-appointed circuit commissioners, those who at the start of the punitive campaign first turned to allegiance and achieved merit—Jiji and Chongtao should be entrusted to reward and appoint them for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: False commissioners who submitted early in the campaign may be rewarded at Jiji's and Chongtao's discretion.

sentences.zh: 其刺史但許稱使君，不得更有檢校官。

translations.literal: Their prefects may only be called "lord prefect"; they may not again hold acting commission titles.
translations.idiomatic: Their prefects may only be called "lord prefect," with no acting commission.

sentences.zh: 其偽署班行正四品已上，酌此降黜，五品已下，如不曾經本朝授官，若材智有聞，即許於府縣中量材任使；

translations.literal: For false court ranks at Regular Fourth and above, demote per this rule; at Fifth and below, if they never received appointment from our dynasty, when talent and wisdom are known permit appointment in prefectures and counties according to ability;
translations.idiomatic: False ranks at Regular Fourth and above are demoted under this rule; Fifth and below without Tang appointment may serve in prefectures and counties if their talent is known;

sentences.zh: 如無材智可錄，止是蜀地土人，並宜放歸田里。

translations.literal: if no talent to record, being only natives of Shu, all should be released to their villages.
translations.idiomatic: those without recordable talent who are only Shu natives should return to their villages.

sentences.zh: 如是西班有稱統軍上將軍者，若是本朝功臣子孫及將相之嗣，並據人材高下，與諸衛小將軍、府率、中郎將，次第授任。

translations.literal: If in the western court there were those styled commander-in-chief or general, if they were descendants of our dynasty's meritorious ministers or heirs of generals and ministers, according to talent high or low grant in succession guards junior general, prefecture commandant, or palace guard lieutenant.
translations.idiomatic: Western "commanders-in-chief" or "generals" who were heirs of Tang merit-holders or ministerial lines should receive guards junior general, prefect commandant, or lieutenant ranks by ability.

sentences.zh: 如是小將軍已下，據人材堪任使者，宜委西川節度使衙前補押衙；

translations.literal: For junior general and below, those whose talent can serve, the Western River military commissioner should supplement as yamen adjutant;
translations.idiomatic: Junior generals and below who can serve may be made yamen adjutants under the Western River commissioner;

sentences.zh: 不堪任使者，亦宜放歸田里。

translations.literal: those unfit to serve should also be released to their villages.
translations.idiomatic: the unfit should also return to their villages.

sentences.zh: 應已前降官，除軍前量事跡任使外，餘並稱前銜，候朝廷續據才行任使。」

translations.literal: For those already demoted, except where the army front appoints them by merit for the moment, the rest keep former titles pending the court's further appointment by conduct and ability."
translations.idiomatic: Previously demoted officers, except those placed at the front by merit, keep former titles until the court appoints them by ability."

sentences.zh: 庚子，彰武、保大等節度使高萬興卒。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Zhangwu and Baoda army military commissioner Gao Wanxing died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Gao Wanxing of Zhangwu and Baoda died.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，淮南楊溥遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Yang Pu of Huainan sent an envoy with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Yang Pu of Huainan sent a tribute envoy.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以晉州節度使李存乂為鄜州節度使，以相州刺史李存確為晉州節度使。

translations.literal: On yisi, Jinzhou military commissioner Li Cuny was made Yanzhou military commissioner, and Xiangzhou prefect Li Cunque was made Jinzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Li Cuny of Jin became Yan commissioner and Li Cunque of Xiang became Jin commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丙午，兩省諫官上疏，請車駕不巡幸汴州，凡三上章，乃允。

translations.literal: On bingwu, remonstrance officials of both provinces submitted memorials asking that the imperial carriage not visit Bianzhou; after three submissions it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu remonstrance officials of both provinces thrice asked that the court not visit Bianzhou, and only then was it granted.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏王繼岌奏，遣秦州副史徐藹齎書招諭南詔蠻。

translations.literal: On gengxu the Prince of Wei Jiji memorialized that he had sent Qinzhou deputy Xu Ai bearing documents to summon and instruct the Nanzhao tribes.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Prince Wei Jiji reported sending Qin deputy Xu Ai with letters to summon the Nanzhao tribes.

sentences.zh: 又奏，點到兩川馬九千五百三十匹。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that the tally of horses from the two rivers was nine thousand five hundred thirty.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported 9,530 horses tallied in the two rivers.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《清異錄》：莊宗滅梁平蜀，誌頗自逸，命蜀匠織十幅無縫錦為被材，被成，賜名「六合被」。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Record of Extraordinary Things》 says: when Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and pacified Shu his ambition grew self-indulgent; he ordered Shu craftsmen to weave a seamless brocade ten panels wide as quilt material; when the quilt was finished he bestowed the name "Cosmos Quilt.")〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Record of Extraordinary Things》 says that after Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and pacified Shu he grew indulgent, had Shu craftsmen weave a ten-panel seamless brocade quilt, and named it the "Cosmos Quilt.")〉

sentences.zh: 辛亥，製皇第二弟存霸可封永王，第三弟存美可封邕王，第四弟存渥可封申王，第五弟存乂可封睦王，第六弟存確可封通王，第七弟存紀可封雅王。

translations.literal: On xinhai, an investiture edict made the Emperor's second younger brother Cunba Prince of Yong (永), the third Cunmei Prince of Yong (邕), the fourth Cunwo Prince of Shen, the fifth Cuny Prince of Mu, the sixth Cunque Prince of Tong, and the seventh Cunji Prince of Ya.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai an investiture edict made Cunba Prince of Yong (永), Cunmei Prince of Yong (邕), Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cuny Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, and Cunji Prince of Ya.

sentences.zh: 是歲，日傍有背氣，凡十三。

translations.literal: That year there were aureoles beside the sun—thirteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: That year solar halos appeared thirteen times.
